title: Second Vatican Council
summary: Pope John XXIII opened the Second Vatican Council at St Peter's on 11 October 1962, hoping for spiritual renewal and an updating (aggiornamento) of the Church's pastoral habits and institutions for the modern world; he called it more pastoral than doctrinal. Representatives of other Christian churches attended as observers. Over four periods the bishops debated greater use of vernacular languages in the liturgy, religious freedom and the Church's attitude to non-Christian religions. Under Paul VI it closed on 8 December 1965 with sixteen documents.

uncertainty.note: Solemn opening in St. Peter's Basilica on 11 October 1962; solemn closing on 8 December 1965.
